author: Ellen G. White
work: Spiritual Gifts, vol. 1 (the corpus copy has no dated title page, so the year comes from the Review notice ARSH September 9,  1858, page 136.10, that the book had been sent to all who ordered it)
text: Both of these important events have their memorials. By partaking of the Lord’s supper, the broken bread and the fruit of the vine, we show forth the Lord’s death until he comes. … The resurrection of Christ is commemorated by our being buried with him by baptism, and raised up out of the watery grave in likeness of his resurrection, to live in newness of life.
note: Principle IV's core in 1858 words: baptism is the memorial of Christ's resurrection, buried with him and raised out of 'the watery grave'.

author: J. N. Andrews
work: History of the Sabbath and First Day of the Week
text: To be buried in the watery grave as our Lord was buried in the tomb, and to be raised from the water to walk in newness of life, as our Lord was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, is the divinely authorized memorial of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And let it be observed, it is not the day of the resurrection, but the resurrection itself, that was thought worthy of commemoration. … It was the resurrection of the Saviour, and not the day of the resurrection, that was worthy of commemoration; and hence burial in baptism was ordained as its memorial.
note: Immersion, not a day, is the God-given memorial of the resurrection; the same paragraph blames the change to sprinkling for the plea for first-day observance.

author: J. H. Waggoner
text: The apostle Paul twice speaks of baptism as a burial. This expression is just according to the meaning of the word immersion. But the term is not well chosen if it is intended to represent sprinkling or pouring. It is likened to the burial and resurrection of Christ, to which the ordinance has undoubted reference.
note: On mode: Paul's 'burial' fits immersion, not sprinkling or pouring (Principle IV: 'no other mode more fitly represents these facts').

author: R. F. Cottrell
text: And as the resurrection of Christ is the pledge of the resurrection of the saints, [1 Corinthians 15:12-18,] so when we, by baptism, confess our faith in the one, as a consequence we confess our faith in the other. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. 1 Thessalonians 4:14. They will be raised from the dead at his coming.
note: Principle IV's last clause: baptism confesses faith in Christ's resurrection and 'as a consequence' in the saints' resurrection at his coming.
